mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during a supply shock.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the effect is absent during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for three consecutive months at > -1% monthly rate
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the effect is reversed during a commodity price surge.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5 percentage points over two months signals a disinflationary tightening, which raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises while CPIAUCSL falls > 0.5pp over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during a credit expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals strengthening household demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both above 12-month moving average simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a fiscal tightening.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate below 6% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as equities reprice for higher growth and inflation.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 6.0% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.8%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect inverts during a wage-price spiral.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) above 0.5% for six consecutive months signals robust consumer demand growth, which lifts corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1.0%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during a simultaneous supply chain disruption.
